claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows 'Nikon' branding on body, confirming brand, but no model number or nameplate detail is visible to confirm 'D810' specifically.
Lens barrel text is illegible in photo 0; focal length and aperture cannot be read.
No shots of LCD, body back, top plate, sensor, or ports are shown to assess cosmetic or functional condition.
Photo 0 clearly shows 'Nikon' branding on the camera body, not Canon.

risks.risk: Seller statement that 'the brand is Canon' directly conflicts with the witness-confirmed Nikon branding, suggesting a copy-pasted or mismatched listing.
risks.proof: A new, clear photo of the camera body and lens together with legible branding and model markings, taken by the seller now.
risks.if_unproven: Treat listing as unreliable; price at worst case as an unverified/possibly misrepresented item until brand and model are reconfirmed.

risks.risk: Actual model (D810 vs any other Nikon body) cannot be confirmed from the photo.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the top LCD or nameplate showing model number.
risks.if_unproven: Price as base unidentified Nikon DSLR body, not as D810.

risks.risk: Lens identity and condition (brand, focal range, aperture, glass/fungus/scratches) unknown.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of lens barrel markings, front and rear glass.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic unknown zoom lens, worst-case condition.

risks.risk: Shutter count/usage history unknown, affecting DSLR value significantly.
risks.proof: Photo or screenshot of shutter count from camera menu or EXIF data tool.

risks.risk: Missing accessories (battery, charger, strap, memory card, box) cannot be confirmed.
risks.proof: Photo of full accessory set laid out together.
risks.if_unproven: Price as body/lens only, no accessories.

risks.risk: Functional defects (autofocus, dials, buttons, sensor dust/scratches) not visible in a static hand-held shot.
risks.proof: Short video showing camera powering on, autofocus working, and a test shot review on LCD.
risks.if_unproven: Price as untested, assume possible faults.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the top plate and LCD showing exact model number
Close-up of lens barrel text for brand, focal length, and aperture
Photo or screen capture of shutter count
Photo of all included accessories (battery, charger, strap, card, box)
Short video of camera powering on and autofocus/shutter operation
A fresh photo consistent with the seller's own description (resolving the Canon/Nikon conflict)
response.reason: The seller's own text claims the brand is Canon while the witness-verified photo clearly shows Nikon branding, a basic factual contradiction that raises strong suspicion of a mismatched or fraudulent listing.
